observation_text: Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) accounts of P5.711 billion out of the total carrying value of P6.734 billion could not be ascertained due to non-completion of the conduct of physical count, and non-reconciliation of the Report of Physical Count of Property, Plant and Equipment (RPCPPE) of the City General Services Office (CGSO) with the City Accounting Office (CAO) records.
recommendation_text:
We reiterate our previous year’s recommendation that:
a. The Local Chief Executive, thru the City Administrator, –
 Instruct the newly created overall Inventory and Reconciliation Committee on PPE accounts to convene, undertake and complete the physical inventory of property, and conduct the reconciliation with the property and accounting records. The committee shall be required to render a report on completion and reconciliation of the PPE accounts within the prescribed timetable; iii
 Require the Procurement Office, to provide the CGSO, upon delivery of the properties, with copies of sales invoice, approved purchase order, distribution list of the PPE supporting the Acceptance and Inspection Report, as their reference in the preparation of the Property Acknowledgement Receipt, Inventory Tag and completion of the RPCPPE;
b. The Property Custodian/Officer, the CGSO and the CAO to –
 Set-up an effective system to keep track and capture the related transactions on PPE; reconcile and adjust PPE records regularly accordingly; and to promptly reconcile the results of the physical count with the accountabilities recorded in the books of accounts and the property cards; and
 Submit the reconciled RPCPPE to the Auditor within the prescribed period mandated in the above COA Circulars.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The non-recording of credit and debit memos and other reconciling items due to lack of documents to substantiate the adjustments, understated the balance of Cash in Bank-Local Currency, Current Account by the net amount of P3.350 million, which includes the unreconciled beginning bank and book balance of P6.408 million.
recommendation_text:
We reiterated our recommendations that:
a. The City Treasurer’s Office (CTO) coordinate with the bank officials on the status of the request for copies of bank credit and debit memos, and other reconciling items for submission to the CAO to support the adjustments;
b. The CAO to –
 Upon receipt of the documents from the CTO, prepare immediately the necessary adjusting entries for the reconciling items; and
 Coordinate with the CTO for the immediate clearing of reconciling items pertaining to the difference of P6,408,293.60 between bank and book beginning balance. The following are the other significant observations and recommedations in the audit of the City of Taguig for CY 2020: iv

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The City was able to exceed its revenue projections for the year by P110.586 million or 1.11 percent amidst the pandemic. The income from Business Taxes still remarkably surpassed the projections for CY 2020 in performance efficiency. We commended Management, in particular the Business Permits and Licensing Office (BPLO) and the CTO, in surpassing the projection for Business Taxes, despite the pandemic in CY 2020.
recommendation_text:
We recommended that the Management, thru the Local Finance Committee (LFC):
a. Involve CTO and other Departments in generating revenues to meet the targets;
b. Require the CTO to accomplish the Quarterly Report of Income to keep track of the status of revenue generation; and
c. Require the concerned officials to conduct periodic review of the Quarterly Report of Income to ascertain whether collection targets are attained to provide assurance of improved finances for the operations of the City.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The City registered a net increase of P92.315 million or .78 percent in the collections during the year as compared with the previous year, despite the COVID-19 pandemic. We commended the Management in the increase of revenues over the last year’s figures, despite the pandemic. However,
recommendation_text:
we still recommend that Management, thru the LFC:
a. Conduct periodic review of its collection efficiency to be assured of improved performance and higher revenues generated. Quarterly review is suggested in order to keep track of revenue accounts that register decline in performance efficiency;
b. Use the revenue targets in the real property taxes to further intensity collections therefrom. Avail of administrative and judicial remedies in enforcing payments particularly in tax delinquencies; and
c. Perform close monitoring of income generated from Permit Fees, Hospital Fees and other fees which decrease in income to ensure efficient collection.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The City's projection of income certified collectible for CY 2020 is presented in summary of receipts or major income account group and not in the itemized or sub-major income or specific receipts classification provided in the Revised Chart of Accounts prescribed in COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015. v
recommendation_text: We recommended that the Management, thru the Local Finance Committee (LFC), involve all the departments/offices concerned for revenue generating activities, in preparation and submission of the report for projected income in order that the necessary details or sub-major income accounts may likewise be rendered by CTO and other LFC members to the City Mayor, in compliance with COA Circular No. 2015-009.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: Official Receipts (ORs) were again issued to acknowledge deductions from tax obligations during the year upon presentation of the Tax Credit Certificates (TCCs) for previous years’ overpayment of taxes, which is inconsistent with the requirements of Sections 67 and 68 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445.
recommendation_text:
We recommended that the CTO:
a. Stop the practice of issuing ORs for TCCs applied for payment of taxes as a deduction from their tax obligations; and
b. Support the Report of Collections and Deposits rendered by collectors with ORs, order of payments/tax bills and copies of the TCCs.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The Acceptance and Inspection Reports and Summary of Supplies and Materials Issued (SSMIs) were not properly substantiated anew to document the recording and utilization of Inventory and related Expense accounts, contrary to the requirements of Section 4(6) of PD No. 1445 and Vol. I of the Manual on New Government Accounting System (MNGAS) for Local Government Units (LGUs).
recommendation_text:
We recommended that compliance with the requirements of Section 4(6) of PD No. 1445 and Sections 118, 119, 116 and 121 of Vol. I of MNGAS for LGUs, be observed as follows:
a. The Local Chief Executive, thru the City Administrator, –
 Instruct the GSO, warehouse keepers and end users’ supply officers to require from suppliers upon delivery of procured items, the copies of delivery receipts bearing the Sales Inovices (SIs) and the related Purchase Order (PO) reference;
 Require the GSO to document acceptance, inspection and recording thru the use of the AIR properly filled up with the necessary information, and complete documentation as to PO reference, SIs/Delivery Receipts (DRs) reference and acceptance by the end user or property officer/warehouse keeper; and
 For the delivered or procured items for CY 2020, instruct the Procurement Office, having the control of the contracts, to submit the delivery receipts vi corresponding to POs and sales invoice attached to the financial transactions to document the recorded Inventory Accounts;
b. The GSO to –
 Require end user and property officer/warehouse keeper to separately prepare and sign an Acceptance Report with POs, DRs and SIs reference of the delivered goods which will document the AIR signed by the GSO Head or Head of Office; and
 Submit to CAO, the monthly SSMI supported with Report of Issued Supplies (RIS) with a duly acknowledged List of Recipients/Distribution List which shall also be indicated with PO/SIs/DRs reference, pictures and other documentation, as basis of the adjustment of Inventory accounts.
c. The Inspection Committee to –
 Comply with the conduct of inspection of the procured items simultaneously with the acceptance of deliveries by the GSO; and
 Require the Chairman, the Committee of Inspection, and the members, who have the field of expertise, to sign the AIR for the delivered goods. For example, for the procured construction materials, the AIR should be signed by the Chairman and the engineer-member, and IT specialist for IT supplies.
d. The CAO to –
 See to it that the recorded inventory accounts will be supported with the AIR, sales invoices with delivery receipts and PO reference; while the recorded utilization or issuance of supplies be documented with SSMI with RIS together with duly acknowledged list of recipients/distribution list, indicating the PO/SIs/DRs reference, pictures and other documentation; and
 To see to it that the recorded delivered or procured items and utilization are supported with the documents required under recommendations a and b, mentioned above.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The City has yet to enact its Revenue Code to consolidate, refine and update 34 ordinances from 1993 to 2020 on the rules and regulations pertaining to its revenue administration system, as well as clarify unclear provisions of the Taguig City Business Tax Ordinance of 2018 on taxes, fees and charges, thus, no ready reference is available for stakeholders, collection implementers and taxpayers. vii
recommendation_text: We reiterated our recommendation that Management consider revision and codification of the City’s revenue rules and regulations in order to have a ready reference for the implementers and the taxpayers. We also recommended that Management coordinate with the Sangguniang Panlungsod to revisit the provisions of the CY 2017 Business Tax Ordinance to come up with amendments that would give a clearer interpretation of revenue provisions.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The City was not able to maximize its revenue raising power by updating/increasing tax impositions on all real property and other fees and charges, as mandated in Sections 191 and 219 of RA No. 7160, hence, rates may no longer be appropriate in the current times and could have an impact in the increase of revenue generation.
recommendation_text: We reiterated our previous year’s recommendation that Management coordinate with the Sangguniang Panlungsod to revisit the provisions of the Taguig Revenue Code, particularly for Schedule of Fair Market Values and other fees and charges to come up with amendments that will redound to the best interest of the government and the citizenry, and introduce new rates that are responsive to the current times.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The collections of City Tax imposed on the sale of real properties by real estate sellers, contractors/developers and financial institutions/banks have no legal basis as there are no provisions on the specific city tax rates to be enacted under the 2017 Revenue Ordinance.
recommendation_text: We reiterated our previous year’s recommendation that the CTO should consider the proposal for the amendments on the provisions of Section 24 of 2017 Revenue Ordinance, to include the specific city tax rates imposition.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The tax rate for Real Estate Business prescribed under Section 12 of Sangguniang Panlungsod Ordinance No. 34, series of 2017, was not uniformly applied on the prior year’s gross receipts/sales declared by certain sellers, dealers or developers of real estate, thus, the reliability of the system, and the accuracy of the business taxes collected from the affected establishments are doubtful.
recommendation_text: We recommended that the CTO as the process owner and the designated IT Office tasked for the activity, effect the uniform application of the tax rate prescribed in the computation of tax for establishments/companies engaged in the business of selling, dealing or developing real properties. We further recommended that the CTO and the IT Office ensure that the automated system computes the tax uniformly for the concerned business establishments, otherwise, we require the submission of the legal basis of the rates of tax imposed other than those prescribed by the Revenue Code. viii

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The City undertook the optimal use and implementation of the revised plans, programs and projects for CY 2020 Local Disaster Risk Reduction Management (LDRRM) Funds of P586.476 million or 99.66 percent to address the disaster response requirements of the COVID-19 emergency. We commended Management for the optimal use and implementation of the revised planned programs and projects of the LDRRM Funds for CY 2020, in addressing the needs of the constituents amidst the COVID-19 pandemic.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The City's 92,472 affected families during pandemic were recipients of the Social Amelioration Program (SAP) out of the transferred funds from the national government in the amount of P739.776 million. There was substantial compliance with the requirements on the grant of financial support to the identified low income families pursuant to Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) Memorandum Circular Nos. 04 and 09, series of 2020, with few exceptions on delays in the liquidation of cash advances and incomplete documentation. We commended Management for the substantial compliance with the requirements on the grant of financial support to the identified low income families pursuant to DSWD Memorandum Circular Nos. 04 and 09, series of 2020. For few exceptions on delays in the liquidation of cash advances and incomplete documentation,
recommendation_text:
we recommended Management to:
a. Require SDOs on the strict adherence to the provisions in COA Circular No. 97-002 dated February 10, 1997, on the full liquidation of cash advances at year-end or as soon as the purpose is served;
b. Request City’s Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO) to adhere with the requirements of Section 4(6) of PD No. 1445, by submitting the required documents such as copies of SACs, IDs/Certifications and Certification from beneficiaries on the acknowledgement of SAP; and
c. Request justification from CSWDO why there were five beneficiaries who received the SAP assistance twice; justification on the changes in the names of SAP beneficiaries in the payroll and why Barangay Tanyag was not provided with a list of SAP beneficiaries for posting purposes.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The City extended P857.150 million financial assistance to 214,573 beneficiaries for various sectors of the community, distributed four waves of relief goods worth P1.351 billion to 375,000 families and provided medical/quarantine facilities of P97.613 million, as response measures to address the COVID-19 pandemic in line with Proclamation No. 922 and RA Nos. 11469 and 11494. ix We recognized and commended the City’s effort in providing its constituents with financial assistance, relief goods assistance and medical/quarantine facilities, as well as RT-PCR testing laboratories, needed this pandemic. The above observations and recommendations were discussed with the concerned City officials and staff on May 5, 2021. Management’s views and comments were incorporated in the report, where appropriate.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The accuracy of the reported balance of Cash-Local Treasury account could not be established due to unreconciled difference of P3.820 million between the accounting books and the City Treasurer’s Office records caused by: (a) incorrect recording in the subsidiary ledgers; (b) unupdated cashbook; and (c) absence of reconciliation contrary to COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015 and Section 26 of the New Government Accounting System (NGAS) Manual for Local Government Units (LGUs), Vol. II.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The Cash in Bank-Local Currency account was overstated by P15.398 million due to: (a) unrecorded/unadjusted book reconciling items in CY 2020 and prior years in the net amount of P21.594 million; (b) non-cancellation of stale checks totaling P4.217 million; (c) inclusion of Deposit in Transit as bank reconciling iii item amounting to P0.027 million; (d) existence of negative balances of two bank accounts totaling P0.991 million; and (e) non-inclusion of City’s five bank accounts totaling P1.014 million.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text:
The reported balance of Cash in Bank account in the Financial Statement as of December 31, 2020, cannot be ascertained due to: (a) non-confirmation of 10 bank accounts totaling P128.646 million; (b) non-submission of the Bank Reconciliation Statements of 14 bank accounts totaling P190.720 million; and
(c) absence of necessary documents supporting the BRS.
recommendation_text:
We recommended that Management require the City Accounting Office to:
a. Coordinate with the PNB, PVB and DBP to determine the nature and details of the 10 unconfirmed bank accounts and also request for the bank statements from the said banks for reconciliation purposes and effect the necessary adjusting entries with complete supporting documents.
b. Submit the BRS with supporting documents of the 14 bank accounts totaling P190,719,730.05 in compliance with Paragraphs 3.2 and 3.4 of COA Circular No. 96-011.
c. Submit copies of the debit/ credit memos, cancelled and paid checks and all other supporting documents for the 35 BRS, in compliance with Paragraph 3.5 of COA Circular No. 96-011.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The Cash in Bank-Local Currency, Current Account (CIB-LCCA) under the Trust Fund totaling P15.831 million has been dormant for more than five years, hence, the existence of the same cannot be ascertained.
recommendation_text: We recommended that Management require the CAO to reconcile its records with the records of the SA, to facilitate the remittance of fund balances to the concerned SA, and the preparation of necessary adjusting entries in the books.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text:
The existence, validity and reliability of Property, Plant and Equipment accounts totaling of P19.402 billion cannot be ascertained due to: (a) unreconciled discrepancies between the accounting records and the Report on the Physical Count of Property, Plant and Equipment (RPCPPE) totaling P1.462 billion; and
(b) unidentified prior years’ balances of P608.885 million.
recommendation_text:
We reiterated our previous year’s recommendation that Management require the:
a. GSO and CAO in coordination with various offices and departments to continuously reconcile their records and make the necessary adjustments;
b. CTO to provide copies of the TCTs to the GSO to facilitate identification and location of the real estate properties of the City; and
c. CAO to determine the composition of the unidentified prior years’ balances in order to determine if the same were fully depreciated and/or no longer existing. v

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text:
The correctness and reliability of the balances of the Construction in Progress accounts in the total amount of P297.743 million could not be ascertained due to:
(a) unidentified beginning balances of P245.524 million; (b) inclusion of completed projects of P18.508 million; and (c) absence of detailed information on accounting entries totaling 33.711 million.
recommendation_text:
We recommended that the Management require the CAO and CED to:
a. Exert more effort to locate the relevant information/documents pertaining to the beginning balances of the CIP accounts in CYs 2012 and prior years;
b. Coordinate with the City Engineers’ office to determine whether the projects implemented in CYs 2014 to 2019 were unfinished or already completed, and prepare accounting entries to transfer the CIP Accounts to the respective asset accounts and compute for the depreciation and accumulated depreciation; and
c. Provide necessary information and copies of the JEVs for the correcting/ adjusting entries, to ensure the accuracy of balances of the CIP and other affected accounts in the financial statements. The following are the other significant findings and recommendations in the audit of the City of Caloocan for CY 2020:

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The City maintains several accounts with the PNB totaling P86.887 million contrary to Section 5.2 of Department of Finance (DOF) Circular No. 01-2017 dated May 11, 2017, thus, exposing government funds to the risk of possible loss in case of bankruptcy of the said private bank.
recommendation_text:
We recommended that Management require the:
a. CAO to request from PNB a copy of the confirmation of balances for all accounts maintained in the said bank, if any, prepare Bank Reconciliation Statements for the five PNB bank accounts and make the necessary adjustments in the books; and
b. CTO to immediately transfer the remaining deposits from PNB, to any of the AGDB listed under Section 5.2 of the DOF DC No. 01-2017.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: Cash advances totaling P80.543 million remained unliquidated as of December 31, 2020, due to the failure of the accountable officer to liquidate the said advances within the prescribed period and non-observance of the guidelines in the granting and liquidation of cash advances under COA Circular No. 97-002 dated February 10, 1997, and Section 89 of PD No. 1445. vi

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: Accounts Payable for General Fund, Special Education Fund and Trust Fund of P25.299 million were outstanding for more than two years without details and supporting documents, hence, the reported balance of the said account in the financial statements is of doubtful validity.
recommendation_text:
We reiterated our previous years’ recommendation that the Management require the CAO to:
a. Analyze and conduct a thorough review of the transactions and their supporting documents and check the existence of actual claimants; and
b. If the transactions were not substantiated with necessary documents and the payable accounts were found to be non-existing without identified valid claimants, the funds intended for the said obligations should be adjusted and reverted to the unappropriated surplus in accordance with the pertinent provisions of PD No. 1445.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: Other Payables account in the Trust Fund (TF) totaling P4.647 million remained dormant for seven years and more, hence, the validity, and reliability of the reported balance in the financial statements cannot be ascertained.
recommendation_text: We recommended that if the payables were proven to be undocumented and without valid claimants, Management should request the Sanggunian to pass a resolution/ordinance to transfer the dormant balances to the General Fund to be utilized for COVID-19 related expenses. vii

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: Out of the fund transfers from National Government Agencies (NGAs) totaling P2.122 billion, P1.938 billion were fully utilized, P75.542 million were partially utilized and P108.622 million were not utilized for intended programs, projects and activities (PPAs), thus depriving the primary beneficiaries/ constituents of the City of the use, benefits and services of the said PPAs.
recommendation_text:
We recommended that Management require:
a. The responsible officials to immediately utilize the funds so that the intended benefits be enjoyed and availed of by the constituents;
b. If already implemented, require the CAO to prepare Fund Utilization Report to eliminate the liability from the Due to NGAs account; and
c. The CAO and CTO to return to the source agencies the unspent balance of the fully implemented PPAs. The aforementioned observations together with the corresponding recommendations were discussed with Management officials concerned during the exit conference on June 18, 2021. Management views and comments were incorporated in the report, where appropriate.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text:
The existence of the City's Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) and the accuracy of the PPE account balances totaling P24.483 billion could not be ascertained due to: (a) incomplete physical inventory count by the Inventory Committee;
(b) non-reconciliation of the Report on the Physical Count of PPE (RPCPPE) with the City Accounting Office (CAO) records; and (c) incomplete maintenance of Real Property Ledger Cards (RPLC), PPE Ledger Cards (PPELC) and Property Cards (PC) contrary to COA rules and regulations casting doubt on the reliability of the reported balances of the PPE accounts in the financial statements as of December 31, 2020.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The balances of Inventories accounts aggregating to P3.114 billion as of December 31, 2020, remained unreliable due to: (a) non-preparation of a complete Report on the Physical Count of Inventories (RPCI); (b) incomplete maintenance of Supplies Ledger Cards (SLCs) and Stock Cards (SCs); and (c) presence of dormant balances in the SLCs which is not in conformity with the provisions of the MNGAS for LGUs.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The Accounts Payable (A/P) and Other Payables (O/P) account balances as of December 31, 2020, included payables that remained outstanding from two to five years amounting to P178.712 million and P16.376 million, respectively, which is not in conformity with Section 98 of PD No. 1445, hence, the validity and propriety of the balances could not be ascertained.
recommendation_text:
We recommended that Management instruct the CAO to -
 Investigate the liabilities without valid/actual claims or found not legitimate which remain dormant/unpaid for two years or more, prepare the corresponding journal entry voucher and revert to the unappropriated surplus of the general fund pursuant to Section 98 of PD No. 1445;
 Prepare the aging of Other Payables account to identify the balances which remain outstanding for two years and more; and
 Prepare and maintain subsidiary ledgers for all payable accounts which were reverted to the general fund for monitoring purpose and future reference in case actual claims will be filed by the respective creditors. vii

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The reported balance of the Investment Property, Buildings (IPB) account as of December 31, 2020, was overstated by P14.762 million due to: (a) the erroneous recording of depreciation in the amount of P4.193 million; and (b) the double recording of an IPB item amounting to P10.568 million which is inconsistent with the provisions of COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015, and the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1 and 16.
recommendation_text:
We recommended that Management direct the CAO to –
 Reclassify the depreciation totaling P4,193,047 to Accumulated Depreciation– Investment Property, Buildings account;
 Prepare the necessary adjustment for the overstatement of P10,568,724 in the Investment Property, Buildings account and understatement of the same amount in the Other Land Improvements account; and
 Reconcile the balances in the SL and LS for the Investment Property, Buildings account in order to provide accurate depreciation for all IPB items pursuant to Paragraph 65 of IPSAS 16.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text:
The correctness of the Construction in Progress (CIP) accounts with a total year-end balance of P1.660 billion could not be ascertained due to the:
(a) non-transfer of the accumulated CIP balances to the respective PPE accounts in the amount of P163.544 million; (b) non-reclassification of completed infrastructure projects to PPE account costing P16.168 million; (c) overstatement of CIP-Buildings by P32.188 million, CIP-Infrastructure Assets – P99.959 million and Accounts Payable by P132.146 million due to erroneous computation of year-end set up of payables and (d) incomplete maintenance of CIP Ledger Cards, all contrary to the provisions of the MNGAS for LGUs, Vol. I, COA Circular No. 2015–009 dated December 01, 2015, and IPSAS 17, resulting in unreliable CIP account balances.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The Cash in Bank-Local Currency, Current Account (LCCA) and Cash in Bank- Local Currency, Savings Account (LCSA) balances per books in the amounts of P3.008 billion and P483.842 million, respectively, as of December 31, 2020, were understated by P5.845 million, due to the unadjusted reconciling items between the GL and bank balances contrary to the provisions of COA Circular No. 96-011 dated October 2, 1996, and Section 74 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The City was not able to reconcile the difference of P444,632,007.23 between the General Ledger (GL) balance of the Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) accounts and the Report on the Physical Count of PPE (RPCPPE) due to the inability of the Accounting and General Services Offices to maintain a complete and updated subsidiary ledgers for each group of PPE and Property Cards, respectively, contrary to Section 269 of Government Accounting Manual (GAM) for Local Government Units (LGUs), Volume I, thereby putting in doubt the reliability of the PPE accounts with carrying value of P3,338,878,858.33 as of December 31, 2020, excluding Construction in Progress.
recommendation_text: For the above-cited deficiencies, 1.a. the Accounting Office to update and maintain the PPE Ledger Cards indicating therein the details of every property acquired by the City, such as the acquisition, description, custody, estimated useful life, depreciation, impairment loss, disposal and other information about the asset; 1.b. the General Services Office to determine the composition of Land Improvements reported in lump-sum, report the results of inventory taking for buildings, structures and public infrastructures in the prescribed RPCPPE and to group the physically counted PPE according to type or category of assets; 1.c. the General Services Office to update and maintain the Property Cards according to account classification; and 1.d. the Accounting and General Services Offices to reconcile their respective PPE records on a regular basis.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The reliability of Construction in Progress - Building and Other Structures account with balance of P124,498,646.53, which was outstanding since December 31, 2018, could not be ascertained due to absence of details pertaining to this account, contrary to Section 111 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 2015-009 dated December 1, 2015.
recommendation_text: For the above-cited deficiencies, 2. the City Accountant to exert effort to retrieve records and analyze the composition and details of Construction in Progress - Buildings and Other Structure account with year-end balance of P124,498,646.53 and make the appropriate adjustments on the books, if necessary;

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: Public Infrastructure Assets of the City with total value of P661,059,371.94 were not provided with depreciation due to absence of subsidiary records for these accounts, contrary to International Public Sector Accounting Standard(IPSAS) 17 and pertinent provisions of the Government Accounting Manual (GAM) for Local Government Units (LGUs), Volume I, thus overstating the Infrastructure Assets and Government Equity accounts by an amount equivalent to the unrecorded depreciation expenses.
recommendation_text:
For the above-cited deficiencies, 3. the City Accountant to -
• retrieve records pertaining to the acquisition of the Public Infrastructures totalling P661,059,371.94;
• prepare and maintain the required Local Road Network Ledger Card (LRNLC) and Other Public Infrastructure Ledger Card (OPILC) for the aforementioned accounts; and iii
• compute and journalize the depreciation of the subject assets from the time of acquisition to present.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: The Other Supplies and Material Inventory account in the Special Education Fund was overstated by P52,970,748.00 while the Other Supplies and Materials Expense account was understated by the same amount, due to improper recording of the receipts and issuances of inventory items, contrary to Sections 175 and 190 of the GAM for LGUs, Volume I.
recommendation_text:
For the above-cited deficiencies, 4. the City Accountant to –
• draw Journal Voucher to adjust the overstatement of Other Supplies and Materials Inventory and Government Equity accounts; and
• be consistent in recording Inventory items by treating these as Assets upon acquisition and to recognize the Expense portion upon the issuances of Inventories.

metadata.document_scope: COA executive summary of the Annual Audit Report

observation_text: Cash balance of P78,991,942.14 in the Special Education Fund (SEF) as of year-end was not sufficient to cover the current liabilities, thus, resulted in cash deficit of P46,292,826.79 attributable to the decrease in the current year’s total income and the increase in current operating expenses and capital expenditures, compared with last year’s, contrary to Section 337 of Republic Act (RA) No. 7160.
recommendation_text: We recommended that the City Budget Officer, Accountant and Treasurer exercise diligence, prudence and proper control in the disposition of government funds by limiting the expenditures within the total income realized during the year to avoid incurrence of cash overdraft. It is likewise recommended that they take concrete and effective measures to cover the cash deficit with the collections in the ensuing year.

observation_text: The City disbursed a total of P292,414,275.46 for purchases of goods and services for COVID-19 operations under emergency procurement authorized under RA No. 11469 without compliance with the documentary requirements provided under Item Nos. 4.1 and 4.3 of Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) Circular No. 01-2020 dated April 6, 2020.
recommendation_text: We recommended that the City Mayor require the City Accountant to coordinate with responsible officials to facilitate the immediate submission to the Commission on Audit of the lacking documents and/or correction of deficiencies noted in audit to prevent suspension and/or disallowance of the transactions. Henceforth, ensure that all required supporting documents are attached to the disbursement vouchers before payment to facilitate the review of the validity and propriety of the disbursement.

observation_text: The manner of recording and reporting the purchase and distribution of the welfare goods amounting to P156,063,376.42 was not in accordance with Commission on Audit (COA) Circular Nos. 2014-002 and 2015-009, thus proper accounting of their receipts, issuances and balances was not facilitated.
recommendation_text:
We recommended that the City Mayor direct the:
▪ City Accountant to properly record the purchases of welfare goods under the account Welfare Goods for Distribution and the distributed portion to Welfare Goods Expenses. He should also maintain Supplies Ledger Cards for all welfare goods; and iv
• City Disaster Risk Reduction Management Officer/City General Services Officer to maintain Stock Cards to record the purchases and issuances of welfare goods. The issuances of these items should be supported with the Requisition Issue Slip (RIS) and reported monthly to the Accounting Office thru the preparation and submission of monthly Report of Supplies and Materials Issued (RSMI) as basis of the City Accountant in recording issued items under account Welfare Goods Expenses.

observation_text: The shares of the Provincial Government of Cavite from the basic real property and special education taxes collected by the City of Bacoor during the year, but which were already due or had accrued prior to cityhood, were not recognized in the books, contrary to Section 111 of PD No. 1445 and Sections 271 and 272 of the Local Government Code, thus understating the Due to LGUs account and overstating the Government Equity account, both in the General and Special Education Funds, by P1,734,655.15 as of year-end.
recommendation_text: We recommended that the City Mayor require the City Accountant to draw Journal Voucher to adjust the understatement in Due to LGUs account and the overstatement of the Government Equity both in General and Special Education Funds. We also recommended that the City Accountant properly recognize the provincial share from the collections of basic real property and special education taxes and penalties thereon, which had become past due prior to its cityhood, in the books of accounts using the account Due to LGUs and maintain the corresponding subsidiary ledger for the Provincial account.

observation_text: The cashbooks for Cash in Local Treasury maintained by the City Treasurer were not always updated, have no running balances, not closed, ruled and certified at the end of each month and not reconciled with Accounting records, contrary to Section 63 of Local Treasury Operations Manual, thus the balances of Cash in Local Treasury could not be easily determined and errors in recording, if any, could not be promptly corrected, thereby affecting the reliability of the recorded transactions and defeated the purpose of maintaining cashbooks.
recommendation_text:
We recommended that the City Mayor require the OIC, City Treasurer to properly maintain the cashbooks by adopting the following suggested measures:
a. Determine the running balance of the cashbook, record transactions daily and reconcile the balance with the actual cash on hand for deposit at the end of each day;
b. Close the cashbooks at the end of the month by double-ruling below the last entries and accomplish the prescribed certification; and
c. Reconcile the cashbook balance with the accounting records and to take up immediately the necessary corrections in the books requiring adjustments.

observation_text: Disposal of various unserviceable motor vehicles of the City with carrying value of P3,403,409.10 was not undertaken. This is contrary to Section 79 of PD No. 1445 and Section 167 of the Rules and Regulations on Supply and Property Management in Local Government Units prescribed under COA Circular No. 92-386 dated October 20, v 1992, thus exposing them to further deterioration and the likelihood of loss or reduction of income from sale of scrap.
recommendation_text: We recommended that the City Mayor instruct the General Services Office (GSO) to expedite the disposal of the unserviceable motor vehicles with total carrying value of P3,403,409.10 in accordance with the aforementioned regulations to halt further deterioration and reduction of their economic values. Upon disposal, the City Accountant should draw a Journal Entry Voucher (JEV) to drop from the books of accounts the cost of the unserviceable motor vehicles. The above observations and recommendations were discussed with the concerned City officials and staff through the exit conference conducted on April 21, 2021. Management’s views and comments were incorporated in the report, where appropriate.
